evaluation_criteria.visual_finish: Reads as shipped product, not wireframe (Stage-2 Design axis)
evaluation_criteria.first_impression_30s: Hackathon judge with 30-sec attention closes pitch in one viewport
evaluation_criteria.brand_voice_consistency: Aggressive YC satire executed with sleek control, not edgelord aggro
evaluation_criteria.accessibility_hygiene: WCAG 2.2 AA — contrast, focus states, semantic HTML, aria attributes
evaluation_criteria.mobile_responsive_viability: Web platform requirement — degrades cleanly to mobile breakpoints
evaluation_criteria.punchline_delivery: 'WHILE YC HIRES, WE SHIP' moment lands on the surface itself

scores.notes: Editorial-grade hero. OKLCH warm-paper palette, oversized 108px display headline with strike-through 'hire,' and gradient 'we ship.' The tilted living preview window with the 71→84→92→96 spec-fit climb IS the proof, IS the punchline, IS the pitch. Float-card dagger quote ('We just shipped theirs') executes the satire with control instead of aggro. Animated progress fill, pulse-dot live indicator, ticker strip — every detail finished. The page itself out-classes the YC sites it mocks; that's the brief.

Clearest 30-second read in the panel. Hero ('They take 6 months. You ship in 24 hours.') with strike-through, single CTA card with prefilled URL, three-step onboarding, live demo strip with agent log, and a 'Their cohort vs You with WhyC' comparison table that quantifies '2,600× faster.' Mobile breakpoint clean. Form labels, aria-labels, semantic landmarks present. Slightly less designed than P05 but converts the punchline into operational receipts faster — a judge could grade this in 20 seconds.

Editorial scroll-story. Serif (Iowan Old Style) display type at 128px, italic 'while they' / orange 'ship,' draggable spec-fit slider as the interactive punchline (judges drag through 71/84/92/96 themselves). Highest production value alongside P05, but density and scroll-to-comprehend cost it on the 30-sec axis. Newspaper-grade typography risks 'student type-spec demo' read if judges don't scroll. Stamp/seal artifact card is genuinely well-crafted.

Honest SaaS dashboard. The 0.92 ← 0.71 hero scoreboard with iter-strip + per-flow judge-note table delivers the killer feature literally: spec-fit climbing in real time IS the product. Linear's design language, no marketing chrome, footer 'while they hire, we ship.' as the only flourish. Strong accessibility (semantic table, aria-hidden SVG, real focus targets). 220px sidebar collapses poorly on mobile. Brand-voice slightly muted — the satire only lands via the footer line.

The meta-satire. Looks like Stripe/Linear console, zero ✨, deterministic 6-stage status pills, real semantic table with badge dots. Best accessibility hygiene in the cohort — WCAG-grade contrast, kbd hints, focus-visible outlines, real form labels. The satire works *because* it doesn't look like an AI demo: 'while YC hires, we ship a real tool that ships things.' Risk: judges may miss the joke entirely and read it as plain-vanilla. Strong inclusion as a hedge — proves the team can build pixel-perfect serious tooling.

chair_vote.rationale: P05 is the only mockup that single-handedly satisfies Stage-2 Design axis success_metric ('WhyC's own UI reads as finished work') AND delivers the punchline in one viewport for a 30-sec judge attention budget. The tilted preview window with the live 71→84→92→96 spec-fit climb is simultaneously the visual hero, the proof of the killer feature, and the satire. Editorial typography (108px display headline, strike-through 'hire,' gradient 'we ship.'), OKLCH warm-paper palette, and the float-card dagger ('We just shipped theirs.') execute aggressive YC satire with surgical control rather than edgelord aggro. The artifact itself out-classes 80% of YC portfolio sites — which is exactly the brief. Every other top-5 candidate optimizes one dimension at the cost of another; P05 is the only Pareto-front pixel.
chair_vote.second_rationale: If P05 fails the 4-day implementation budget, P03 is the safe ship: same punchline, simpler IA, faster to build, comparison-table receipts, mobile-clean.

dissent.issue: oklch(38% 0.012 60) ink-soft body text on warm paper is borderline 4.5:1 — verify before ship; add focus-visible outlines on .nav-cta and .btn-primary.
1.05fr/.95fr hero grid collapses to 1fr at 960px but float-card absolute positioning on bottom-right at mobile risks overlap with metrics row.
Single-fold-everything is high-risk: no scroll narrative, no FAQ, no how-it-works deeper dive — judges who want to inspect convergence cannot.
Editorial scroll-story requires scroll engagement; 30-sec judges may bounce before reaching the spec-fit slider punchline.
Anti-AI minimalism may read as 'forgot to design the hero' to judges scanning for visual ambition on the Design axis.
220px fixed sidebar and 1fr/360px main split have no mobile breakpoint declared — dashboard breaks below 900px.
'2,600× faster' microcopy in comparison table risks reading as marketing-superlative; trim to 'minutes vs months' for honest-tone consistency.
Chat-as-product surface (excluded from top-5) reads as Cursor/Claude clone — no distinct visual identity for WhyC; satire gets lost in the chat shell.
@keyframes fill at 2.4s ease may feel slow on first paint; consider 1.6s with staggered loop-strip step delays for tighter perceived performance.
Mobile-only mockup (excluded from top-5) is a fragment — needs a desktop counterpart since hackathon judges grade on web platform first.

panel_consensus_summary: P05 chair-vote is consensus across Designer/Visual/Motion/End-User/Brand-Voice/Content-Designer/Usability-Tester lenses. Accessibility-Advocate, IA, and Mobile-UX lenses register dissent on single-fold risk and contrast hygiene — fixable with targeted polish, not architecture changes. P03 unanimously the fallback. P18 wins pure-design but loses 30-sec test. P11 wins killer-feature literalism. P26 wins accessibility but bets the joke on judge sophistication.
implementation_notes_for_M3: If shipping P05: tighten oklch ink-soft contrast to ≥4.6:1, add explicit :focus-visible outlines on .nav-cta/.btn-primary/.btn-ghost, verify float-card mobile reposition, reduce @keyframes fill duration to 1.6s.
If shipping P03: keep comparison table but soften '2,600× faster' microcopy; add explicit empty/error/loading states for the live demo strip.
If hybrid: P05 hero + P03 comparison-table-and-demo-strip below the fold = best of both punchline density and operational receipts.

Required across all winners: real semantic <main>/<nav>/<section> landmarks, alt-text on all decorative SVGs (use aria-hidden), keyboard-traversable form, prefers-reduced-motion override for animated fill/pulse.

axis_alignment_with_idea_spec.spec_success_metric_design: both WhyC's own UI and the generated previews read as finished work
axis_alignment_with_idea_spec.evaluation: P05 directly satisfies — the tilted preview window inside the hero IS the 'generated preview reading as finished work' demonstration AND the WhyC UI itself. Single-mockup compliance with the dual-finish requirement.
axis_alignment_with_idea_spec.spec_brand_tone: 픽셀 퍼펙트 sleek UI, 진지하게 끝난 작품처럼 (브루털리즘 아님)
axis_alignment_with_idea_spec.evaluation: P05 OKLCH warm-paper + editorial typography hits 'sleek finished work' precisely; explicitly not brutalist. P18 also compliant. P11/P26 read as 'serious tool' more than 'finished art piece.' P03 sits in the middle.

P05, P11, P13, P18 all surface the climb literally. P05 makes it the visual hero; P11 makes it the entire dashboard; P18 makes it interactive (slider). All three are spec-faithful — P05 just executes with the highest visual finish.
